\subsection*{Input files}
\begin{description}
\item[\texttt{--freq-file} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] A file of allele frequencies for every variant, with one frequency column per population headed by its label, or a single column that applies to every population: CHR SNP POS ALLELE FREQ \textless{}chr\textgreater{} \textless{}locus ID\textgreater{} \textless{}pos\textgreater{} \textless{}allele\textgreater{} \textless{}freq\textgreater{} By default the frequencies are calculated from the data. The .freq.gz that a run writes can be given back here. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{none}
\item[\texttt{--gl-beagle} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] Genotype likelihoods in beagle format, as written by ANGSD -doGlf 2: a header of marker, allele1, allele2 and three columns per individual, then one row per site with P(reads | allele1/allele1), P(reads | allele1/allele2) and P(reads | allele2/allele2). This is the input for low-coverage sequence data. The per-site term of the LOD score is averaged over the three genotypes, weighted by the likelihoods, so an uncertain site contributes little evidence and a site with no reads (a flat triplet) contributes exactly 0. Replaces \texttt{--tped} and \texttt{--vcf}. \texttt{--tfam} is still required and is matched to the beagle columns by position (the order of ANGSD's -b bam list). \texttt{--error} is still required. It is the chance that a site inside a run looks non-autozygous for any reason, while the likelihoods carry the read-level uncertainty, so \texttt{--gl-type} is refused. Allele frequencies are estimated by EM over the likelihoods, and \texttt{--freq-file} overrides them. Run ANGSD on an ascertained site list (-sites, or at least -SNP\_pval). Give likelihoods, not -doPost or -doGeno posteriors, which already include a Hardy-Weinberg prior. \texttt{--weighted} and \texttt{--cm} still need \texttt{--map}. See the manual for its limits at low depth. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{none}
\item[\texttt{--gl-type} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] Which genotype-quality field to use. With \texttt{--vcf} it is read from the FORMAT column. With \texttt{--tgls} it names the form of the single value per genotype in the .tgls file. The two are not equivalent. With \texttt{--vcf} (recommended): GQ error = 10\textasciicircum{}(-GQ/10), as the VCF specification defines it. PL The whole PL array is converted to a posterior:     P(g) proportional to 10\textasciicircum{}(-PL\_g/10),  error = 1 - P(called)/sum.   A VCF normalises PL so that the called genotype's value is 0 for   every call, and the information is in how much worse the   alternatives are. GL The same, via PL = -10*GL.   A missing field is an error that names whichever of GQ, PL and GL   the file does carry, and '.' for a called genotype is an error. With \texttt{--tgls} (legacy, one value per genotype): GQ As above. The only form a VCF's values can be used in directly. PL error = 1 - 10\textasciicircum{}(-PL/10), where 10\textasciicircum{}(-PL/10) is P(genotype correct).   This is not the VCF PL field. Integer PLs give errors of 0, 0.21,   0.37, 0.50, ..., and an error of 0.001 is PL = 0.00435. VCF PLs   given here are rejected. Use \texttt{--vcf} \texttt{--gl-type} PL instead. GL error = 1 - 10\textasciicircum{}GL, with the same caveat. Below roughly 4x, use \texttt{--gl-beagle}. Each form above gives one error rate per genotype, evaluated at the called genotype, so an uncertain homozygous call still counts as evidence for autozygosity. See "Low-coverage sequence data" in the manual. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{none}
\item[\texttt{--map} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] A scaffold genetic map. Sites not in the file are interpolated, and sites outside its bounds are dropped. Required by \texttt{--weighted} and \texttt{--cm}. Format: \textless{}chr\textgreater{} \textless{}snpid\textgreater{} \textless{}genetic pos\textgreater{} \textless{}physical pos\textgreater{}. Negative positions are an error. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{none}
\item[\texttt{--tfam} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] A TFAM file holding population and individual IDs. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{none}
\item[\texttt{--tgls} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] A tgls file with one per-genotype value per individual, in the row order of the TPED. See \texttt{--gl-type} for what the values mean. For PL and GL this is not the VCF convention. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{none}
\item[\texttt{--tped} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] A TPED file holding the map and the genotypes. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{none}
\item[\texttt{--tped-missing} \textnormal{\textless{}char\textgreater{}}] The one-character missing-data code in a TPED. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{0}
\item[\texttt{--vcf} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] A VCF file (plain, gzipped or BGZF) to read genotypes from instead of \texttt{--tped}. Biallelic SNVs with a GT field are used. Multiallelic sites, indels and symbolic ALTs are skipped, and the counts are reported. Sample names come from the \#CHROM line, so \texttt{--tfam} is not accepted. Use \texttt{--pop} for population labels. Sites must be grouped by chromosome. Ploidy must be 2, except on a chromosome declared with \texttt{--sex-system} or \texttt{--sex-chr}, where a haploid call is read as hemizygous. With \texttt{--phased} every call must use '|'. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{none}
\item[\texttt{--vcf-pass-only} \textnormal{\textless{}bool\textgreater{}}] Skip sites whose FILTER is neither PASS nor '.'. Without this flag such sites are kept and their number is reported, because FILTER records the variant caller's thresholds rather than garlic's. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{false}
\end{description}
\subsection*{Populations}
\begin{description}
\item[\texttt{--pool-populations} \textnormal{\textless{}bool\textgreater{}}] Analyse every individual as one population, ignoring the labels, as garlic did before per-population analysis. Output names are then \textless{}out\textgreater{}.roh.bed rather than \textless{}out\textgreater{}.\textless{}POP\textgreater{}.roh.bed. Allele frequencies are pooled over everyone, which inflates heterozygosity relative to any one population and biases the LOD scores. Use it when the labels are not populations (column 1 of a TFAM is the PLINK family ID) or to reproduce an earlier run. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{false}
\item[\texttt{--pop} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] A file mapping sample ID to population, in place of the labels in the TFAM. Whitespace separated, '\#' comments and blank lines ignored, .gz accepted:   \textless{}sample\_id\textgreater{}  \textless{}population\textgreater{}  [sex] The column order is the reverse of a TFAM's first two columns. The optional third column is sex in PLINK coding (1 male, 2 female, 0 or -9 unknown). Unlike in a TFAM, any other value is an error. Rows are matched by sample ID, not by order. Every sample in the data needs a row. Extra rows are ignored and counted, so one file can be used for a subset of the cohort. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{none}
\end{description}
\subsection*{Genome and chromosomes}
\begin{description}
\item[\texttt{--autosomes-only} \textnormal{\textless{}bool\textgreater{}}] Drop every chromosome that is not an autosome before calling: X, Y, Z, W and the mitochondrion by name, and 23, 24, 25 and 26 when \texttt{--build} names a human assembly. A hemizygous chromosome analysed as an autosome is called as one run along its whole length. Without a human \texttt{--build}, bare 23-26 are refused rather than dropped, because they are autosomes in a species with that many chromosomes. See \texttt{--sex-system}. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{false}
\item[\texttt{--build} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] The genome build: hg18, hg19, hg38 or t2t-chm13 (T2T-CHM13v2.0, UCSC hs1). It supplies the centromere locations, the chromosome lengths and the human pseudoautosomal regions. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{none}
\item[\texttt{--centromere} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] A file of custom centromere boundaries, \textless{}chr\textgreater{} \textless{}start\textgreater{} \textless{}end\textgreater{}. One of \texttt{--build}, \texttt{--centromere} or \texttt{--no-centromere} is required. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{none}
\item[\texttt{--chr} \textnormal{\textless{}string1\textgreater{} ... \textless{}stringN\textgreater{}}] Analyse only these chromosomes, e.g. \texttt{--chr} chr1 chr2 chrX. Names are matched after normalisation, so '1' and 'chr1' are the same. Naming a chromosome that is not in the data is an error. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{all chromosomes in the input}
\item[\texttt{--chr-lengths} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] A file of chromosome lengths in two whitespace-separated columns, chromosome and length. A samtools faidx .fai is accepted as it is. Needed for \texttt{--froh-denominator} assembly on a non-human assembly or on TPED input, where nothing in the data states a length. Takes precedence over \texttt{--build} and a VCF's \#\#contig header. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{none}
\item[\texttt{--exclude-regions} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] A BED file of regions whose sites are dropped before anything is computed, such as a mappability or repeat mask or segmental duplications. Mapping bias in such regions turns heterozygotes into homozygotes, which looks like autozygosity. Standard BED (0-based half-open \textless{}chrom\textgreater{} \textless{}chromStart\textgreater{} \textless{}chromEnd\textgreater{}, further columns ignored, track/browser/\# lines skipped), gzipped or not. Chromosomes not in the data are ignored. The dropped sites are removed from the frequency file and from every window, but the FROH denominator is not reduced (unlike \texttt{--par}). Applied on every chromosome. Use \texttt{--par} for pseudoautosomal regions. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{none}
\item[\texttt{--haploid-chr} \textnormal{\textless{}string1\textgreater{} ... \textless{}stringN\textgreater{}}] Chromosomes haploid in every individual (mitochondrion, chloroplast). Dropped before calling. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{names matching M or MT, plus 26 under a human --build}
\item[\texttt{--no-centromere} \textnormal{\textless{}bool\textgreater{}}] Treat every chromosome as having no assembly gap, instead of requiring \texttt{--build} or \texttt{--centromere}. For assemblies with no centromere gap, and for references with no built-in table. Cannot be combined with \texttt{--build} or \texttt{--centromere}. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{false}
\item[\texttt{--par} \textnormal{\textless{}string1\textgreater{} ... \textless{}stringN\textgreater{}}] Pseudoautosomal regions on the shared sex chromosome, as \textless{}chr\textgreater{}:\textless{}start\textgreater{}-\textless{}end\textgreater{}, comma or space separated. The loci inside are dropped, since the regions are diploid in both sexes and too short to call. Any number of regions per chromosome is allowed. Coordinates are in the input's assembly, and a region cannot be named by chromosome code, because PLINK's 25 is an ordinary autosome in most species. \texttt{--build} supplies the human X regions from the Genome Reference Consortium's definition (see centromeres/par\_regions.txt). Naming any region here replaces them, and \texttt{--par} none turns them off. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{the regions for --build, or none without one}
\item[\texttt{--par-file} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] The same regions read from a file, one per line as \textless{}chr\textgreater{} \textless{}start\textgreater{} \textless{}end\textgreater{}, with '\#' comments and blank lines ignored and .gz accepted. Unlike \texttt{--centromere}, repeated rows for a chromosome add a region. May be combined with \texttt{--par}. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{none}
\item[\texttt{--sex-chr} \textnormal{\textless{}string1\textgreater{} ... \textless{}stringN\textgreater{}}] The chromosome that is diploid in the homogametic sex and hemizygous in the heterogametic one (X under xy, Z under zw). Needed only when it has another name, e.g. \texttt{--sex-system} zw \texttt{--sex-chr} LG12. Requires \texttt{--sex-system}. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{the conventional name for --sex-system}
\item[\texttt{--sex-chr-degenerate} \textnormal{\textless{}string1\textgreater{} ... \textless{}stringN\textgreater{}}] The chromosome carried only by the heterogametic sex (Y under xy, W under zw). It is dropped before calling, since no individual can carry a run of homozygosity on it. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{the conventional name for --sex-system}
\item[\texttt{--sex-system} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] Which sex is heterogametic, and so which individuals are hemizygous on the shared sex chromosome:   xy    individuals coded 1 (male) in the TFAM or \texttt{--pop} are heterogametic   zw    individuals coded 2 (female) are heterogametic   none  every chromosome is diploid in every individual, and sex         chromosomes are not reported PLINK codes 1 male and 2 female in every species, so in a ZW species the homogametic sex is coded 1. Leaving the flag unset is not the same as 'none'. If a sex chromosome is present and the flag is unset, garlic stops rather than analysing it as an autosome. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{unset}
\end{description}
\subsection*{LOD scores and windows}
\begin{description}
\item[\texttt{--M} \textnormal{\textless{}int\textgreater{}}] The expected number of meioses since a recent common ancestor, for \texttt{--weighted}. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{7}
\item[\texttt{--auto-winsize} \textnormal{\textless{}bool\textgreater{}}] Choose the window size automatically. With \texttt{--weighted} it is set from SNP density (see \texttt{--auto-winsize-coef}). Otherwise the search starts at \texttt{--winsize}, which must be given, and grows by \texttt{--auto-winsize-step} SNPs until the LOD score density meets \texttt{--auto-winsize-threshold}, up to \texttt{--max-winsize}. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{false}
\item[\texttt{--auto-winsize-coef} \textnormal{\textless{}double1\textgreater{} ... \textless{}doubleN\textgreater{}}] \textless{}slope\textgreater{} \textless{}intercept\textgreater{}: coefficients of winsize = slope*log(density) + intercept, used by \texttt{--auto-winsize} with \texttt{--weighted}. The defaults are an empirical fit to human SNP-array data. Change them for other ascertainment schemes or species. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{8.3235 138.0521}
\item[\texttt{--auto-winsize-step} \textnormal{\textless{}int\textgreater{}}] The step size, in SNPs, of the \texttt{--auto-winsize} search. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{10}
\item[\texttt{--auto-winsize-threshold} \textnormal{\textless{}double\textgreater{}}] The smoothness criterion at which the \texttt{--auto-winsize} search stops. Lower values demand a smoother LOD score density, and so a larger window. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{0.5}
\item[\texttt{--error} \textnormal{\textless{}double\textgreater{}}] The assumed genotyping error rate. Required. With \texttt{--gl-beagle} it is the chance that a site inside a run looks non-autozygous for any reason (see \texttt{--gl-beagle}). \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{-1}
\item[\texttt{--max-gap} \textnormal{\textless{}int\textgreater{}}] No LOD score window is calculated across a gap between two loci larger than this many bp. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{200000}
\item[\texttt{--max-winsize} \textnormal{\textless{}int\textgreater{}}] The largest window size that \texttt{--auto-winsize} will try. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{1000}
\item[\texttt{--mu} \textnormal{\textless{}double\textgreater{}}] The mutation rate per bp per generation, for \texttt{--weighted}. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{1e-09}
\item[\texttt{--phased} \textnormal{\textless{}bool\textgreater{}}] The data are phased. Under \texttt{--weighted}, LD is then computed as r2 rather than hr2, which uses more memory. With \texttt{--vcf} every call must use '|'. Has no effect on the LOD scores without \texttt{--weighted}. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{false}
\item[\texttt{--weighted} \textnormal{\textless{}bool\textgreater{}}] Weight the LOD scores by LD and by the probabilities of no recombination and no mutation (wLOD). Requires \texttt{--map}. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{false}
\item[\texttt{--winsize} \textnormal{\textless{}int\textgreater{}}] The window size, in SNPs, over which LOD scores are calculated. With \texttt{--auto-winsize} it is where the search starts. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{0}
\item[\texttt{--winsize-multi} \textnormal{\textless{}int1\textgreater{} ... \textless{}intN\textgreater{}}] Several window sizes, in SNPs. garlic writes the LOD score KDE for each and calls no ROH. With \texttt{--auto-winsize} it chooses the best size from the list. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{-1}
\end{description}
\subsection*{Calling runs of homozygosity}
\begin{description}
\item[\texttt{--auto-overlap-coef} \textnormal{\textless{}double1\textgreater{} ... \textless{}doubleN\textgreater{}}] \textless{}slope\textgreater{} \textless{}intercept\textgreater{}: coefficients of overlap\% = slope*log(density) + intercept, used by \texttt{--auto-overlap-frac}. The defaults are an empirical fit to human SNP-array data. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{6.375 63.888}
\item[\texttt{--auto-overlap-frac} \textnormal{\textless{}bool\textgreater{}}] Choose \texttt{--overlap-frac} from marker density (see \texttt{--auto-overlap-coef}). \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{false}
\item[\texttt{--het-rate-bounds} \textnormal{\textless{}double1\textgreater{} ... \textless{}doubleN\textgreater{}}] \textless{}lo\textgreater{} \textless{}hi\textgreater{}: heterozygosity on the shared sex chromosome below which an individual reads as hemizygous and above which it reads as diploid. In between it is ambiguous, and garlic neither calls ROH there for that individual nor counts its alleles. Used to check each recorded sex and to infer the missing ones. The bounds are fixed rather than fitted, because a cohort of one sex has no bimodality to fit. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{0.020000}
\item[\texttt{--ld-subsample} \textnormal{\textless{}int\textgreater{}}] The number of individuals sampled at random for the LD calculations of \texttt{--weighted}. If the population has fewer, all are used. 0 or less uses every individual, which takes longer. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{0}
\item[\texttt{--lod-cutoff} \textnormal{\textless{}double\textgreater{}}] A LOD score cutoff above which windows are called autozygous, applied to every population. By default it is chosen automatically from the KDE of the LOD scores. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{-999999}
\item[\texttt{--overlap-frac} \textnormal{\textless{}double\textgreater{}}] The fraction of the windows covering a SNP that must be above the LOD cutoff for the SNP to be in a run. Runs are therefore at least WINSIZE*OVERLAP\_FRAC SNPs long. If 0, garlic uses the smallest sensible value, 1/winsize. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{0.25}
\item[\texttt{--sexchr-lod-cutoff} \textnormal{\textless{}double\textgreater{}}] Call the shared sex chromosome at this LOD score cutoff instead of the autosomal one. Every run logs the cutoff that the sex chromosome's own windows would give, which is where a value for this comes from. The autosomal cutoff is the default because one chromosome's windows from part of a cohort often have no second minimum in the density. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{the autosomal cutoff}
\item[\texttt{--sexchr-winsize} \textnormal{\textless{}int\textgreater{}}] Use windows of this many SNPs on the shared sex chromosome instead of the autosomal size. The overlap fraction is unchanged. A LOD score cutoff is specific to the window size it was estimated at, so \texttt{--sexchr-lod-cutoff} is required as well. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{the autosomal window size}
\end{description}
\subsection*{Choosing the LOD cutoff automatically}
\begin{description}
\item[\texttt{--kde-cut} \textnormal{\textless{}double\textgreater{}}] Extend the density grid this many bandwidths beyond the range of the data. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{3}
\item[\texttt{--kde-points} \textnormal{\textless{}int\textgreater{}}] The number of grid points at which the LOD score density is evaluated. This also sets the resolution of the LOD cutoff. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{512}
\item[\texttt{--kde-subsample} \textnormal{\textless{}int\textgreater{}}] The number of individuals sampled at random for the LOD score KDE. If the population has fewer, all are used. The default, 0, uses every individual, so the cutoff depends on the data alone. A positive value saves memory but makes the cutoff depend on \texttt{--seed}. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{0}
\item[\texttt{--kde-thin-step} \textnormal{\textless{}int\textgreater{}}] Send every Nth LOD score window to the KDE. 0, the default, uses the window size, so the windows used do not overlap. 1 uses every window. \texttt{--no-kde-thinning} is a deprecated alias for 1. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{0}
\item[\texttt{--mode-smooth-span} \textnormal{\textless{}int\textgreater{}}] The number of adjacent grid points used to smooth the density when finding its modes. Must be smaller than \texttt{--kde-points}. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{20}
\item[\texttt{--no-kde-thinning} \textnormal{\textless{}bool\textgreater{}}] Deprecated. The same as \texttt{--kde-thin-step} 1, which sends every LOD score window to the KDE and can increase runtime considerably. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{false}
\item[\texttt{--stratify-cutoff} \textnormal{\textless{}bool\textgreater{}}] Choose the automatic LOD cutoff within strata of individuals that carry the same evidence per window, so that the shallow members of a cohort of mixed depth are not over-called. Individuals are sorted by the location of their non-autozygous LOD mode, neighbours whose modes differ by less than a quarter of the smaller spread share a stratum, and the pooled rule is applied within each stratum. A cohort of uniform depth is one stratum and gets exactly the pooled cutoff. The per-individual mode, spread, stratum and cutoff are written to \textless{}out\textgreater{}.ind.tsv. Needs the automatic cutoff. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{false}
\end{description}
\subsection*{Size classification}
\begin{description}
\item[\texttt{--cm} \textnormal{\textless{}bool\textgreater{}}] Report ROH lengths and size classes in cM. ROH boundaries are still reported in bp. Requires \texttt{--map}. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{false}
\item[\texttt{--gmm-max-iter} \textnormal{\textless{}int\textgreater{}}] The maximum number of EM iterations when fitting ROH size classes. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{1000}
\item[\texttt{--gmm-tol} \textnormal{\textless{}double\textgreater{}}] The convergence tolerance of the ROH size-class EM fit. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{1e-05}
\item[\texttt{--nclust} \textnormal{\textless{}int\textgreater{}}] The number of Gaussian mixture components used to classify ROH lengths. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{3}
\item[\texttt{--size-bounds} \textnormal{\textless{}double1\textgreater{} ... \textless{}doubleN\textgreater{}}] The boundaries between ROH size classes, in increasing order. By default they are chosen automatically with a Gaussian mixture model (see \texttt{--nclust}). \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{-1.000000}
\end{description}
\subsection*{Counting classified genotypes}
\begin{description}
\item[\texttt{--features} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] A file classifying sites, in four whitespace-separated columns:   \textless{}chr\textgreater{} \textless{}pos\textgreater{} \textless{}allele\textgreater{} \textless{}class\textgreater{} Lines beginning '\#' are comments. Class labels are arbitrary text, and there may be any number of them. A site may appear more than once, so two annotation schemes can classify the same variant, but the same class twice at one site is an error. Chromosome names are matched ignoring case and a 'chr' prefix. For each individual garlic counts the classified genotypes inside runs of each size class and outside them, and writes \textless{}out\textgreater{}.counts.tsv. Genotypes are read from the input the run was called from, or from \texttt{--tped-counting} or \texttt{--vcf-counting} if given. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{none}
\item[\texttt{--roh-file} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] Count classified genotypes against the calls in an existing garlic .roh.bed instead of calling ROH. \texttt{--tped} and \texttt{--vcf} are not used. Give the genotypes with \texttt{--tped-counting} and \texttt{--tfam-counting} or with \texttt{--vcf-counting}, and the classification with \texttt{--features}. A .roh.bed does not record which chromosomes were analysed or what the size class letters mean, so no site can be marked UNASSESSED and the size class boundaries are reported as unknown. Counting inside the run that makes the calls knows both. garlic 1.1.6a was released with two chromStart conventions under one version string, so the convention is inferred from the file and reported. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{none}
\item[\texttt{--tfam-counting} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] The TFAM naming the samples in \texttt{--tped-counting}, in column order. Individuals are matched to the ROH calls by ID, and one present in only one of the two files is reported and left out of the table. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{none}
\item[\texttt{--tped-counting} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] A TPED to count classified genotypes from, instead of the file the run was called from, for example when the calls come from array data and the classified variants are sequenced. The two need not share a single site. Requires \texttt{--tfam-counting} and \texttt{--features}. These genotypes take no part in calling and are not filtered, since monomorphic and rare sites are what is being counted. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{none}
\item[\texttt{--vcf-counting} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] A VCF to count classified genotypes from, instead of the file the run was called from. Sample names come from its \#CHROM line. Requires \texttt{--features}. Unlike the VCF a run is called from, indels and multiallelic sites are read here. The classified allele is matched against REF and every ALT, so a classification that is not a biallelic SNV still counts. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{none}
\end{description}
\subsection*{Output}
\begin{description}
\item[\texttt{--force} \textnormal{\textless{}bool\textgreater{}}] Overwrite existing output files. Without it garlic will not overwrite an existing \textless{}out\textgreater{}.roh.bed. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{false}
\item[\texttt{--freq-only} \textnormal{\textless{}bool\textgreater{}}] Write the frequency file from the data and exit. Uses little memory. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{false}
\item[\texttt{--froh} \textnormal{\textless{}bool\textgreater{}}] Also write \textless{}out\textgreater{}.froh.tsv, with each individual's autozygous total and fraction by ROH size class. The denominator is stated in the header. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{false}
\item[\texttt{--froh-denominator} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] What \textless{}out\textgreater{}.froh.tsv divides the autozygous total by. analyzed (default): the span the markers cover, from the first to the last locus of each analysed chromosome, less the centromere and any region excluded with \texttt{--par}. It moves with the marker set, so FROH from two different arrays are not directly comparable. assembly: the full length of each analysed chromosome, as published FROH denominators use. Lengths come from \texttt{--chr-lengths}, \texttt{--build} or a VCF's \#\#contig header, in that order, and a chromosome with no length stops the run. Not available with \texttt{--cm}. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{analyzed}
\item[\texttt{--out} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] The base name for all output files. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{outfile}
\item[\texttt{--outdir} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] Write all output files to this directory, which is created if needed. The same as prefixing \texttt{--out} with the path.
\item[\texttt{--raw-lod} \textnormal{\textless{}bool\textgreater{}}] Also write the LOD scores to gzip-compressed files. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{false}
\end{description}
\subsection*{Run control}
\begin{description}
\item[\texttt{--dump-docs} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] Write the command line reference to stdout and exit: txt for the README block, tex for the manual's appendix. Used by 'make docs'. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{\_\_none}
\item[\texttt{--help} \textnormal{\textless{}bool\textgreater{}}] Prints this help dialog. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{false}
\item[\texttt{--load-params} \textnormal{\textless{}string\textgreater{}}] Read flag values from a \textless{}out\textgreater{}.params.json written by an earlier run. Flags on the command line take precedence, so a run can be repeated with one parameter changed. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{\_\_none}
\item[\texttt{--quiet} \textnormal{\textless{}bool\textgreater{}}] Suppress the progress bar and informational messages. Errors and warnings still go to stderr and to \textless{}out\textgreater{}.error. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{false}
\item[\texttt{--resample} \textnormal{\textless{}int\textgreater{}}] The number of resamples for estimating allele frequencies. If 0, garlic uses the frequencies calculated from the data. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{0}
\item[\texttt{--seed} \textnormal{\textless{}int\textgreater{}}] The random seed. Affects \texttt{--kde-subsample}, \texttt{--ld-subsample} and \texttt{--resample}. If 0 (the default), a seed is drawn and written to the log so that the run can be repeated exactly. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{0}
\item[\texttt{--threads} \textnormal{\textless{}int\textgreater{}}] The number of threads for the LOD scores, the LD calculations under \texttt{--weighted}, the LOD score KDE and ROH assembly. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{1}
\item[\texttt{--verbose} \textnormal{\textless{}bool\textgreater{}}] Show the progress bar even when stderr is not a terminal. By default it is shown only on a terminal, because it is drawn with backspaces. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{false}
\item[\texttt{--version} \textnormal{\textless{}bool\textgreater{}}] Print the version and exit. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{false}
\item[\texttt{-h} \textnormal{\textless{}bool\textgreater{}}] Prints this help dialog. \\ \textit{Default:} \texttt{false}
\end{description}
\endgroup
